title: Degree-zero normalization of the fixed large module comparison
statement: For any scheme X [def-pc-scheme], any sheaf F of O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and any section s over X, apply the degree-zero right-derived global-sections unit [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] to s, then the fixed moduleAbelianCohomologyLarge comparison [def-pbc-canonical-coherent-etale-comparison]. Its terminal Zariski section evaluation sourceZero is exactly s. This is a formula for the fixed comparison, without any quasi-coherence, nonemptiness, compactness, separatedness or field assumption.

source.place: Tag 03FD; homology.tex Tag 015E; derived-categories.tex Tag 06XR, degree-zero resolution and Ext computations

proof.text: For any additive functor, the degree-zero derived unit, followed by the injective-resolution comparison, is the augmentation into cycles followed by the cycle-to-homology map. Exact forgetting of scalars preserves this formula, by the natural cycles and homology comparison maps.

For the underlying abelian sheaf, the forgotten module resolution is section-acyclic. Naturality of the canonical acyclic-resolution comparison, checked after mapping to a chosen injective resolution, identifies the same augmentation formula. The fixed Ext/sections comparison sends the Ext class of a degree-zero morphism to the associated section cocycle. The terminal-source identification evaluates its free generator at the integer 1.

Evaluate the defining natural-isomorphism composite first for arbitrary functors. The module-to-abelian-section component preserves the derived-unit morphism by the common-resolution augmentation square. Independently, the inverse site-section component followed by terminal Ext-source change sends the abelian derived unit to the inverse H.equiv_0 image of the section: cancel the site-section isomorphism using the terminal generator evaluation. Compose these two unit identities and evaluate at the original section. This uses the defining components directly, without unfolding a chosen resolution or invoking the separate Ext-to-sections factorization theorem.

For Ext in either presentation universe, homAddEquiv sends mk_0(f) to the same degree-zero derived morphism. Thus universe transport preserves addEquiv_0 and consequently preserves the constant-sheaf-adjunction terminal evaluation H.equiv_0. Apply this to the fixed comparison to obtain the asserted formula.

theorem moduleAbelianCohomologyLarge_zero (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : X.Modules) (s : Γ(F, ⊤)) :
    letI : EnoughInjectives (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) :=
      (RingedSpace.moduleSheaves_abelian_enoughInjectives X.toRingedSpace).2
    CoherentEtale.sourceZero X F
      (moduleAbelianCohomologyLarge X F 0
        ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).toRightDerivedZero.app F s)) =
      s
